slides.title: Compile-Time Selection with if constexpr
slides.prompt: Introduced in C++17, if constexpr allows conditional compilation where discarded branches are completely ignored and not compiled for incompatible types.

slides.title: if constexpr Syntax

options: if constexpr

slides.title: Discarded Branch Behavior
slides.prompt: What happens to the discarded branch of an if constexpr statement during compilation?
options: It is completely excluded from instantiation for that particular type
It is compiled normally but skipped at runtime
It causes compile errors if it contains invalid syntax
It is moved to a separate dynamic translation unit
slides.correctAnswer: It is completely excluded from instantiation for that particular type

slides.title: if constexpr vs Regular if
slides.prompt: Why would *t fail in a regular if (std::is_pointer_v<T>) statement when T is int?
options: Both branches are compiled, so *t causes a compile error because int cannot be dereferenced
Regular if cannot evaluate type traits
The condition evaluates at runtime instead of compile time
Non-pointer types cause stack overflow in standard if blocks
slides.correctAnswer: Both branches are compiled, so *t causes a compile error because int cannot be dereferenced

slides.title: Syntax Checking in Discarded Branches
slides.prompt: Are non-dependent syntax errors checked inside discarded if constexpr branches?
options: Yes, non-dependent syntax errors are checked even in discarded branches
No, discarded branches are completely skipped by the lexer
Only if debug flags are set in the compiler
Syntax is checked during linking phase
slides.correctAnswer: Yes, non-dependent syntax errors are checked even in discarded branches

slides.title: Replacing SFINAE with if constexpr
slides.prompt: How does if constexpr improve over SFINAE for handling type-specific behavior?
options: It places conditional logic inside a single function instead of requiring multiple overloads
It speeds up execution time by running in multithreaded mode
It eliminates the need for template headers
It bypasses compile-time type safety checks
slides.correctAnswer: It places conditional logic inside a single function instead of requiring multiple overloads
